answer: Diversity in Pottery Form collapses and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneously at BCE 1700 (the 17th century BCE), with a secondary inflection at BCE 1000 (the 10th century BCE) where Decoration rises further while Form stays collapsed.

payload.hypothesis: Diversity in Pottery Form collapses and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneously at BCE 1700 (the 17th century BCE), with a secondary inflection at BCE 1000 (the 10th century BCE) where Decoration rises further while Form stays collapsed.
payload.workflow: Loaded the raw 37-bin century series PotteryForm and PotteryDecoration from time_series_data.csv (CE -4100..-500, 100-year bins). Computed 100-yr deltas. Applied thresholds with the active 37-bin sigma (Form std=0.98, Decoration std=0.86): collapse = drop <= -1.0 sigma with new floor <= -1.0 sustained for >= 4 consecutive bins; increase = rise >= +1.0 sigma with new plateau >= +0.7 sustained for >= 3 consecutive bins. Skipped BCE 4300/4200 leading bins (saturation floors with no baseline). Cross-checked against capital.csv ZKeform/Zkeverz (identical deltas at BCE 1700). Re-ran detection using the 3601-row _inter std as sensitivity test (same result). Identified BCE 1000 secondary inflection where Decoration fresh-steps +0.97 -> +1.53 while Form remains floored. No detrending applied (cols already Z-standardized). _inter columns used only as sanity check; saturation-floor clipping confirmed pushed apparent transition to ~CE -1750 so they were not primary.
